settings.intro: Every quotation is priced from these rates. Sales still quote in a minute from the defaults; the survey and managers fill in the detail. A change applies to new quotations only; accepted ones keep their own figures.

lines.intro: One line for everything you price: each cable size, conduit or tray, structure part, kit, crew day, equipment hire and service. Add a line here and it can be used on any site type or quotation.
lines.caption: Rate lines
lines.sites: {count, plural, one {# site type} other {# site types}}

sheet.description: What it is, how it is counted, and what it costs and sells for.
sheet.label: Name
sheet.labelHint: As it should read on the bill of materials, e.g. DC cable 6 sq mm.
sheet.kindHint: Decides where it sits on the quotation and in the cost build-up.
sheet.unitHint: m, nos, set, day, kW or job.
sheet.productHint: When it is a stock item: the store reserves it for the project and its catalog price applies.
sheet.catalogPrice: Priced from the catalog: {price} per {unit}, cost {cost}. Change it in Settings → Products.
sheet.inUse: Used in {count, plural, one {# place} other {# places}}; remove it there before deleting it.

editors.noParts: No parts: the structure is priced per kW from its benchmark.
editors.noCrew: No crew: labour is priced per kW on every job.

sites.intro: What a quick quote assumes about each kind of site until the survey measures it. A structure with parts is priced from its real components; without parts it uses its per-kW benchmark.
sites.caption: Site types
sites.crew: {people, plural, one {# person} other {# people}}, {pace} kW a day

sheet.description: Defaults for this kind of site. The survey or a manager can change any of them on a quotation.
sheet.structureHint: Its parts, counted per panel, per row of panels, per gap between two panels in a row, per kW or per job. Legs can grow with the height.
sheet.label: Name on the quotation
sheet.labelHint: Used when the structure is priced per kW.
sheet.benchmarkHint: Used only when the structure has no parts.
sheet.routesHint: Before the survey: metres across the roof, plus a drop for every floor, times the cables sharing the route.
sheet.crewHint: People by skill, paid per person-day. Days follow the size of the system, never fewer than the minimum.
sheet.equipmentHint: Scaffolding, lifting and the like, needed from a floor up (0 for every job).

labour.jobItemsHint: Kits, per-kW installation and the DISCOM work every system needs.
labour.noJobItems: Nothing is added to every job.
labour.floorsHint: Extra labour per kW for each floor above the free floors.
labour.travelHint: Charged once for each site visit, on its own line: never inside labour, so no distance is charged twice.
labour.roadFactorHint: Times the straight line from the base to the site.
labour.baseHint: Where crews and material leave from. With it, quotations fill in the distance to any site that has GPS. In Google Maps, right-click the office to copy its numbers.
labour.accessHint: Extra labour when a site is hard to work on. Easy sites add nothing.

accessLevels.difficult: Difficult (no stairs, crane or rope work)

rules.pricingHint: Either each rate and product carries its own selling price, or the price follows from cost.

modeHints.rates: Each rate line and catalog product sells at its own price. Overhead and the target margin are used to show the true margin.
modeHints.margin: Every engine line sells at cost × (1 + overhead) ÷ (1 − target margin). Hand-added lines keep their own prices.

rules.allowancesHint: What covers the unknown before the survey, and what needs a manager.

hints.marginBp: Share of the price before GST left after all cost and overhead.
hints.overheadBp: Office and running costs, added on top of the direct cost of each job.
hints.contingencyBp: Added to quantities from site-type defaults, to cover what the survey may find.
hints.toleranceBp: Cost changes within this band after the survey are absorbed; beyond it, a revision needs approval.
hints.discountApprovalBp: Discounts larger than this share of the price need a manager's approval.
hints.wastageBp: Added to every metre of cable and routing for cuts and loops.
hints.sqmPerKwp: After the survey, a roof with less shadow-free area than this per kWp gets a revision sized to fit. 0 switches the check off.
hints.goodsTaxBp: On panels, structure, cable and kits.

builder.gpsDistance: Filled in from GPS: about {km} km by road. Change it if the road is longer.
builder.noBase: Set the base location in Settings → Rates to fill this in from the site's GPS.

detail.toggle: Site detail: cable runs, structure, crew and visits
detail.waiting: The detail appears once the price is worked out.
detail.intro: What the price assumes for this site. Change anything the survey measured; that part then counts as measured and carries no contingency.
detail.inverterPlaceholder: e.g. Ground floor, near the meter
detail.runsHint: Floor by floor and route by route; wastage is added. {metres} m of cable in all.

notANumber.floor: Type the floor as a whole number, like 2.
notANumber.acrossM: Type metres as a number, like 12.5.
notANumber.upM: Type metres as a number, like 6.
notANumber.runs: Type how many cables as a whole number, like 2.

detail.structurePerKw: No parts on this site type, so it is priced per kW. Add parts to price it from its components.
detail.structureHint: {rows, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}} of up to {perRow} panels, priced from its parts.
detail.labourHint: Crew days are added to the labour on every job. Each visit is one trip from base ({trip}), charged once.
detail.visitsHint: Each is one trip from base.

modes.rates: Prices from each rate and product.
modes.margin: Prices from cost plus the target margin.

facts.runsMeasured: Measured run by run ({count, plural, one {# run} other {# runs}})
